skill.name: artifacts-builder
skill.description: Build complex Claude HTML artifacts with a React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and shadcn/ui project workflow.
skill.summary: Scaffold and bundle React-based HTML artifacts for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
skill.author: ArtemisAI

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally relies on shell scripts to scaffold, install dependencies, edit project configuration, and bundle React artifacts. Most Markdown, JSDoc, hardcoded URL, and bounded filesystem alerts are safe context, but community shell execution and dependency installation remain meaningful review concerns.

remediation.issue: Unpinned package downloads and global package-manager installation
remediation.suggestion: Pin package versions, avoid npm install -g when possible, and document all network installs before execution.

remediation.issue: Shell scripts create projects and modify local configuration files
remediation.suggestion: Validate project names, reject path-like inputs, and tell users to run the scripts only inside a disposable workspace.

remediation.issue: Packaged shadcn component archive is opaque to simple static review
remediation.suggestion: Prefer checked-in source files or publish an archive checksum and manifest for easier review.

remediation.issue: Bundling cleanup deletes dist and bundle.html in the current project
remediation.suggestion: Print cleanup targets before deletion and keep cleanup limited to an explicit build directory.

semantic_findings.title: Package Installation During Skill Execution
semantic_findings.description: The setup and bundling scripts install pnpm globally and download multiple npm packages while the skill is being used. This creates supply-chain and reproducibility risk for a community skill.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The lines directly invoke npm or pnpm install commands, including a global pnpm install and package downloads. This is expected for the skill, but it is still a real supply-chain risk.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Build Cleanup Command
semantic_findings.description: The bundling script removes dist and bundle.html before building. The targets are relative and expected, but running the script in the wrong project can delete local build output.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The rm command is visible and hardcoded to project-local paths after basic project checks. The bounded scope lowers severity, but deletion behavior should still be disclosed.

content.value_statement: Complex artifacts often outgrow single-file HTML and become hard to maintain. This skill creates a React project workflow and bundles it into one shareable HTML artifact.
actual_capabilities: Creates a React 18, TypeScript, and Vite project from a shell script.
Installs Tailwind CSS, Radix UI, lucide-react, and shadcn/ui dependencies.
Configures Tailwind theme variables, path aliases, and Vite alias support.
Extracts packaged shadcn/ui component source files into the project.
Bundles the project into one self-contained HTML file with Parcel and html-inline.
limitations: Requires Node.js 18 or newer and access to npm package installation.
Runs shell scripts that modify local project files and install dependencies.
Best suited for complex interactive artifacts, not simple static snippets.
The bundled component archive should be trusted before running the setup script.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Artifact Project
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new interactive artifact.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a new React artifact project named dashboard-demo. Keep the default stack and explain the generated files.

prompt_templates.title: Build with shadcn/ui Components
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate UI development with included components.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a React artifact that uses shadcn/ui buttons, cards, tabs, and dialogs. Keep the layout responsive and ready for bundling.

prompt_templates.title: Bundle an Existing Project
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert a completed artifact project into one HTML file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the artifact bundling workflow for this project and report the output file name, expected usage, and any build issues.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Package a Complex Artifact
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow before sharing a production-style artifact.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React artifact for missing dependencies, styling issues, and bundle readiness. Then prepare the self-contained HTML artifact.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a project scaffold for an interactive analytics artifact.
output_examples.output: A new React and TypeScript project is created with Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui components, and path aliases ready for development.

output_examples.input: A user asks to package a finished artifact for sharing.
output_examples.output: The project is built with Parcel and converted into a single HTML file that includes the required scripts and styles.

output_examples.input: A user asks whether the skill is appropriate for a one-screen static mockup.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends a simpler single-file artifact unless the project needs state, routing, or reusable component structure.

best_practices: Use this skill when the artifact needs stateful React components or a larger UI structure.
Review generated package changes before running install or bundle commands.
Open and test the final HTML artifact before sharing it with users.
anti_patterns: Do not use the full scaffold for a small static HTML response.
Do not run the scripts in a directory with unrelated project files.
Do not trust bundled archives or installed packages without source review.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and shadcn/ui project for complex HTML artifacts.

faq.question: Can it produce one shareable HTML file?
faq.answer: Yes. The bundling script builds the project and inlines assets into bundle.html.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: Usually yes. The scripts install npm packages unless dependencies are already available locally.

faq.question: Is it compatible with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: When should I avoid it?
faq.answer: Avoid it for simple single-file artifacts that do not need React state or component structure.

faq.question: What should I review before use?
faq.answer: Review the shell scripts, package installs, and included component archive before running setup.
